description: Market steam-closing line value interaction with rest advantage: CLV differential multiplied by steam intensity, conditioned on rest days differential. Detects when sharp money aligns with schedule edges.
hypothesis: Market microstructure signals are amplified when one team has rest advantage; sharp money moves faster on fresher teams, creating predictive CLV-rest interaction.

description: Clutch momentum bayesian update: Posterior probability of clutch performance derived from pre-game EMA of clutch net rating and prior from season-long clutch sample, weighted by clutch minutes volume.
hypothesis: Small-sample clutch stats are noisy; bayesian shrinkage toward prior, with volume-based confidence, yields more stable clutch predictions than raw clutch ratings.

description: Heterogeneous stacking with recency-weighted base learners and neural network meta-learner incorporating prediction uncertainty estimates
hypothesis: Current stacking underweights model reliability drift—XGBoost excels early season, FT-Transformer mid-season, LightGBM playoffs. A meta-learner that receives both base predictions AND estimated prediction uncertainties (via MC dropout for neural nets, quantile regression for trees) can dynamically reweight ensemble contributions. Neural network meta-learner captures non-linear interactions between base model disagreements and game context.

description: Closing line value (CLV) interaction with market steam and rest disparity: sharp money captured by CLV combined with late line movement direction and rest advantage
hypothesis: CLV alone is polluted by public bias; when combined with steam (late sharp money) and rest context, it identifies true sharp positions vs. square positions. Rest amplifies CLV signal due to market inefficiency in pricing fatigue.

description: Deep FT-Transformer with attention on player embeddings to capture complex team interaction patterns beyond tree-based feature engineering
hypothesis: Transformer attention mechanisms will better model non-linear player synergies and lineup interactions that tree ensembles miss, especially for injury-adjusted predictions

description: Heterogeneous stacking ensemble with diverse base learners and ridge meta-learner to reduce correlated errors
hypothesis: Combining gradient-boosted trees (XGB/LGBM/CatBoost) with neural approaches (TabNet/MLP) and regularized meta-learner will exploit complementary strengths and smooth overconfident predictions

description: Opponent-adjusted four factors EMA crossover with rest-weighted recency: Calculate exponential moving averages (fast=7, slow=15) of opponent-adjusted eFG%, TOV%, ORB%, FTr for each team, then compute crossover signals (fast-slow) weighted by days rest (less rest = higher weight to fast EMA for fatigue-sensitive stats like TOV%)
hypothesis: Teams on short rest exhibit amplified momentum in fatigue-sensitive four factors; EMA crossovers capture trend inflections better than rolling windows, and opponent-adjustment removes schedule noise

description: Referee-specific market steam absorption rate: Measure how efficiently closing line value (CLV) is captured when steam moves align with referee tendencies (high-foul refs = steam on overs absorbed faster; low-foul refs = steam on unders), creating a market microstructure inefficiency score
hypothesis: Referee styles create predictable market friction; steam moves in direction of referee bias are under-reacted to due to public focus on teams not officials, creating exploitable CLV gaps

description: Clutch-player availability momentum divergence: Interaction between team clutch performance trend (5-game EMA of clutch net rating) and key player availability volatility (rolling std dev of minutes-weighted RAPTOR availability), capturing how uncertainty in star presence affects late-game execution
hypothesis: Markets underprice the interaction between clutch momentum and roster uncertainty; teams with rising clutch trend but high availability volatility present asymmetric upside when stars unexpectedly play

description: FT-Transformer with learned feature interactions on hierarchical four-factors embeddings. Uses transformer attention to model complex non-linear relationships between opponent-adjusted metrics and market signals without manual feature engineering.
hypothesis: Self-attention mechanisms will capture latent interactions between team momentum, player availability clusters, and market regime shifts that gradient boosting misses due to greedy tree splits. The learned embeddings will generalize better to rare game states (back-to-backs, playoff atmospheres).

description: CatBoost with ordered boosting on high-cardinality categorical features (referee-venue combinations, player injury clusters, market steam direction buckets). Explicitly models categorical interactions without one-hot explosion.
hypothesis: Ordered boosting reduces prediction shift and handles categorical features (referee styles, venue-specific market behaviors) more robustly than XGB/LGBM. The symmetry-aware splits will better isolate referee-venue-market interaction effects that showed promise in prior tests.

description: Two-level stacking: Level-1 uses XGBoost (momentum features), LightGBM (market features), CatBoost (categorical interactions), TabNet (sparse attention on player-level data). Level-2 logistic regression with CV-fold predictions and Bayesian calibration.
hypothesis: Model diversity through architecture heterogeneity (tree vs neural attention vs explicit categorical handling) captures complementary signal. The meta-learner optimally weights predictions based on feature subspace reliability, while calibration corrects systematic overconfidence in tail probabilities (clutch games, heavy favorites).

description: Referee-clutch microstructure interaction: referee foul tendency z-score in clutch × team free throw momentum × late-game line movement steam
hypothesis: Referee clutch bias is nonlinear and amplified when teams have FT momentum; market steam in final 2 hours reflects sharp awareness of this, creating exploitable discontinuity

description: Schedule-compressed venue altitude interaction: rest-adjusted back-to-back fatigue × altitude differential × market opening line error
hypothesis: Altitude effects are systematically underestimated in compressed schedules; market opening lines lag schedule announcement timing, creating serial correlation in pricing errors exploitable via interaction

description: FT-Transformer with learned embeddings for team-pair interactions and time-aware positional encoding, processing raw player availability sequences as tokenized inputs rather than engineered aggregates
hypothesis: Preceding FT-Transformer test showed promise; this variant replaces hand-crafted temporal features with learned representations of injury reports, lineup volatility, and team-specific rhythm patterns, allowing the transformer to discover latent team-state representations

description: Clutch market divergence: absolute difference between CLV and actual win probability in late-and-close games, interacted with rest advantage and referee tendency toward home team
hypothesis: Markets systematically misprice clutch performance; when combined with physical fatigue (rest) and referee home bias, creates exploitable situational edges that raw CLV misses

description: Microstructure steam decay velocity: rate of line movement in final 2 hours before close, interacted with reverse line movement indicator and sharp money concentration
hypothesis: The speed and direction of late market moves contains information about informed vs. uninformed money; velocity × reverse movement identifies sharp action that models typically underweight

description: Test the performance of a TabNet model with embeddings on team and player statistics
hypothesis: The TabNet model will outperform the current best model by effectively capturing complex interactions between team and player statistics

description: Evaluate the effectiveness of a CatBoost model with attention on opponent strength and home-court advantage
hypothesis: The CatBoost model with attention will improve predictions by emphasizing the impact of opponent strength and home-court advantage on game outcomes

description: Investigate the potential of a FT-Transformer model with multi-head attention on temporal game data
hypothesis: The FT-Transformer model with multi-head attention will enhance forecast accuracy by modeling temporal dependencies and relationships in game data

description: Closing line value microstructure asymmetry: Decompose CLV into opening-to-midpoint and midpoint-to-closing movements, weighted by volume proxies. Measure divergence between sharp (early) and public (late) money signals, interacted with team rest advantage.
hypothesis: Sharp money captured in early line moves has higher predictive power than late steam; the interaction with rest reveals when market overreacts to fatigue narratives versus genuine information.

description: FT-Transformer with temporal positional encoding and hierarchical pooling: Extend learned feature interactions with sinusoidal positional encodings for game recency (days since game) and hierarchical pooling that aggregates player-level embeddings to team-level before final prediction head.
hypothesis: Explicit temporal structure + proper hierarchical aggregation will capture roster construction effects (star depth vs. top-heavy teams) that flat feature interactions miss, reducing Brier on games with injury uncertainty.

description: Three-level stacking with uncertainty-weighted meta-learner: Level-1: XGBoost (momentum features), LightGBM (market features), CatBoost (roster features). Level-2: Per-model uncertainty estimates via quantile regression. Level-3: Meta-learner weights predictions by inverse predicted variance, with explicit regularization against overconfident base models.
hypothesis: Uncertainty-aware stacking will outperform uniform or learned-weight stacking by downweighting base models when their predicted distribution shows high variance, crucial for edge cases (back-to-backs, trade deadline games).

description: Opponent-adjusted four factors momentum spread: Rolling EMA of (team_four_factor - opponent_allowed_four_factor) weighted by recency, crossed with market closing line value to detect when sharp money disagrees with fundamental trend
hypothesis: Teams showing improving opponent-adjusted efficiency margins that diverge from CLV direction indicate mispricing; the interaction captures when market lags fundamental momentum shifts

description: Referee-game state microstructure: Referee foul differential tendency in clutch (last 5 min, within 5 pts) interacted with team foul-drawing rate volatility and steam move magnitude in final 15 minutes before tip
hypothesis: Referees with high clutch foul variance create non-linear scoring environments; when combined with late steam against public-heavy teams, this captures systematic referee-market inefficiencies

description: Schedule-compressed player impact decay: Cumulative minutes-weighted player BPM (box plus-minus) over 7 days, adjusted for travel distance and rest days, interacted with opponent defensive versatility index
hypothesis: Star-heavy teams suffer asymmetric fatigue under compressed schedules that opponent-adjusted stats miss; the interaction with defensive versatility captures when tired offenses face switchable defenses

description: FT-Transformer with multi-head self-attention over tabular features, treating each feature as a token in a sequence with learned positional embeddings for temporal structure
hypothesis: The previous FT-Transformer test showed promise; this enhanced version with deeper attention layers (4 blocks) and feature-wise embeddings will capture non-linear interactions between team statistics, player availability, and schedule density that tree models miss

description: Hierarchical stacking ensemble with specialized base learners for distinct game contexts: one stack for regular-season games, one for playoffs, with a gating meta-learner that weights predictions based on game importance and team experience
hypothesis: NBA dynamics differ fundamentally between regular season and playoffs; by training context-specialized base models (XGBoost for regular season pattern stability, CatBoost for playoff small-sample adaptation) and learning optimal combination weights, we reduce Brier score on the heterogeneous distribution

description: Opponent-adjusted four factors momentum: rolling offensive/defensive rating differentials adjusted for opponent strength, weighted by recency via EMA decay
hypothesis: Raw four factors are noisy; opponent-adjusted differentials with exponential decay capture true team quality trends better than simple rolling averages, especially for teams facing variable schedule strength

description: Referee-player interaction microstructure: referee foul tendency z-score multiplied by team free throw rate sensitivity, conditioned on clutch time market pressure
hypothesis: Referee impact is non-linear and depends on team playing style; high-FT-rate teams facing whistle-happy refs in tight games see amplified market inefficiency not fully priced into closing lines

description: Venue-rest-market triple interaction: home court advantage EMA multiplied by rest differential, with cross-term against early line movement direction
hypothesis: HCA is systematically mispriced when rest asymmetries interact with venue elevation/travel; sharp early money captures this before market converges, leaving residual edge in the divergence pattern

description: FT-Transformer with learned feature interactions and early stopping on validation Brier, using attention dropout to prevent overfitting on noisy market microstructure signals
hypothesis: Transformers can capture non-linear interactions between clutch divergence and steam decay velocity better than tree ensembles; attention mechanisms will weight situational features dynamically by game context

description: CatBoost with ordered boosting and custom loss function targeting Brier score directly, exploiting its native handling of categorical game contexts (back-to-back, rest days, playoff implications)
hypothesis: Ordered boosting reduces target leakage in small-sample NBA situations; native categorical support eliminates manual encoding of situational buckets; direct Brier optimization aligns training with evaluation metric

description: Bayesian rest-venue-market convergence: Bayesian updating of team true talent (prior: season-long SRS, likelihood: last 10g point differential) interacted with rest advantage (days rest diff) and venue altitude/timezone crossing, then compared to closing line residual. Identifies when market overreacts to schedule noise vs. signal.
Testing TabNet with embedded categoric features
hypothesis: TabNet can effectively handle high-dimensional categoric data and improve Brier score

description: Evaluating FT-Transformer with multi-resolution temporal encoding
hypothesis: Multi-resolution temporal encoding can capture more nuanced patterns in game data and reduce Brier score

description: Market microstructure momentum divergence: Interaction between closing line value (CLV) direction and team momentum spread, capturing when market movement conflicts with recent performance trends
hypothesis: Games where market steam opposes team momentum (e.g., line moving against hot team) create exploitable inefficiencies due to public overreaction to recent results

description: Referee-player impact microstructure: Interaction between referee foul-calling tendency and player foul-drawing/generation rates, adjusted for game-state compression
hypothesis: Specific referee-player matchup effects are amplified in high-leverage moments and create systematic free throw attempt differentials

description: Heterogeneous stacking with domain-specialized base learners: defensive-efficiency specialist (CatBoost on opponent-adjusted metrics), clutch-performance specialist (XGBoost on last-5-minute splits), and schedule-fatigue specialist (LightGBM on rest/travel features), merged via quantile-regression meta-learner
hypothesis: Different game contexts require different predictive signals; by forcing base learners to specialize on distinct basketball domains rather than competing on full feature space, the meta-learner receives uncorrelated, complementary predictions that capture distinct winning pathways (defensive grind vs. clutch execution vs. schedule advantage)

description: Market microstructure momentum divergence: closing line value (CLV) residual unexplained by public betting splits, interacted with steam move direction and time-to-close, capturing sharp money detection vs. public overreaction
hypothesis: CLV alone is noisy; the signal-to-noise ratio improves when conditioning on whether line movement occurred with or against public money, and how late it occurred—late steam against public indicates informed money, early steam with public indicates overreaction

description: Stacked ensemble with XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost base learners and Ridge meta-learner, trained on out-of-fold predictions with 5-fold stratified CV. Base models optimized for calibration via isotonic regression on validation folds before meta-training.
hypothesis: Combining gradient boosting variants with different optimization objectives (Newton-Raphson vs leaf-wise vs ordered boosting) captures complementary error patterns. Ridge meta-learner prevents overfitting to base model correlations. Targeting 0.195 Brier through variance reduction without bias introduction.

description: FT-Transformer with decoupled attention heads for player-level and team-level features, plus learned uncertainty quantification via evidential output layer. Incorporates temporal positional encoding for schedule density and explicit rest-day embeddings.
hypothesis: Previous FT-Transformer underperformed due to homogeneous treatment of hierarchical features (player stats nested within teams). Decoupled attention separates granular player interactions from team macro patterns. Evidential deep learning outputs Dirichlet parameters enabling aleatoric uncertainty modeling, critical for close games where Brier score is most sensitive.

description: LightGBM with quantile-based gradient boosting and custom Brier loss approximation via Taylor expansion to 3rd order. Features include learned embeddings from pre-trained autoencoder on 5-season player trajectory sequences.
hypothesis: Standard gradient boosting uses 2nd-order Taylor expansion; 3rd-order captures skewness in win probability residuals for extreme underdogs/favorites where Brier is non-symmetric. Pre-trained player trajectory embeddings encode career arc information (aging curves, development spikes) unavailable in static features. Quantile-based splits handle heavy-tailed player performance distributions.

description: Rest-schedule-market microstructure triple interaction: Combine days rest differential with schedule density (games in last 7 days) and steam move detection (sudden line shifts >1 point). Captures fatigue amplification when sharp money aggressively corrects lines on tired teams.
hypothesis: Steam moves against fatigued teams (high schedule density + rest disadvantage) are stronger signals than steam moves alone; the interaction identifies market overcorrections and sharp exploitation of situational edges.

description: FT-Transformer with learned attention pooling over player-level sequences and team-level aggregation via cross-attention mechanism, replacing manual hierarchical fusion with end-to-end differentiable attention that learns optimal player-to-team contribution weights dynamically
hypothesis: Manual hierarchical aggregation loses fine-grained player contribution signals; learned cross-attention between player sequences and team representations will capture contextual player importance (star vs bench performance) and reduce Brier by 0.015+ through richer representation learning

description: TabNet with sparsemax attention and entmax-1.5 activation for sharper feature selection, combined with ghost batch normalization and a novel sequential decision step that mimics coach substitution patterns—each step attends to different game-phase features (early/late, clutch, blowout)
hypothesis: Standard TabNet uses softmax which dilutes attention; entmax-1.5 induces sparser, more interpretable selections. Structuring decision steps around game phases aligns inductive bias with basketball dynamics, improving calibration on edge cases (close games, back-to-backs)

description: Deep stacking ensemble with heterogeneous base learners (XGBoost with monotonic constraints, LightGBM with GOSS sampling, CatBoost with ordered boosting) feeding into a quantile-regression neural network meta-learner that explicitly models prediction uncertainty for weighted combination
hypothesis: Current stacking uses point estimates; quantile-aware meta-learner learns when each base model is overconfident vs underconfident, enabling adaptive weighting that reduces Brier on volatile matchups (injury uncertainty, rest advantage mismatches) where single models fail

description: Closing line value microstructure with rest asymmetry: Interaction between CLV direction, line movement velocity in final 2 hours, and rest differential. Tests whether sharp money identification varies by schedule advantage.
hypothesis: CLV contains stronger predictive signal when rest differential favors the team receiving sharp money; tired teams failing to cover CLV indicates true market inefficiency vs. fatigue discounting.

description: FT-Transformer with Mixup augmentation and MLP-Mixer-style token mixing: Replace standard transformer blocks with factorized attention (attention across features, then across samples) plus Mixup regularization on embedding space. Adds learnable feature embeddings for continuous variables with periodic activation for temporal features.
hypothesis: Previous FT-Transformer underperformed due to overfitting on small NBA sample sizes. Mixup in embedding space creates synthetic training examples that preserve game-structure relationships. Factorized attention reduces quadratic complexity while maintaining cross-feature interactions critical for lineup chemistry modeling.

description: Hierarchical Stacking with uncertainty-weighted meta-learner: Three-tier architecture. Tier 1: Domain-specific base learners (XGBoost for box-score features, LightGBM for tracking data, CatBoost for categorical-heavy market/ref features). Tier 2: Middle ensemble per domain with out-of-fold predictions. Tier 3: Meta-learner is probabilistic (Bayesian Ridge) that weights base predictions by estimated epistemic uncertainty from each domain.
hypothesis: Previous stacking ensembles failed by treating all base learners equally. NBA prediction uncertainty varies systematically by data domain—tracking data is noisy for fast breaks, market data is reliable late in season. Uncertainty-weighted meta-learner adapts combination weights per-game based on which domains are trustworthy, directly targeting Brier score decomposition.

description: Rest-adjusted referee bias interaction: referee home/away foul differential tendency (20-game history) multiplied by rest differential (team rest days minus opponent rest days), conditioned on back-to-back flags. Captures when tired teams face refs with systematic whistle patterns.
hypothesis: Referee effects are amplified under fatigue; rest differentials interact non-linearly with referee tendencies to create exploitable market inefficiencies in totals and spreads.

description: Clutch-market microstructure divergence: 4th quarter/OT performance EMA (weighted by leverage index) minus implied clutch performance from closing line movement patterns (steam direction in final 2 hours). Flags when market overreacts to or ignores recent high-leverage execution.
hypothesis: Markets overweight narrative-driven clutch performance; quantifying the gap between actual clutch EMA and market-implied clutch skill reveals mean-reversion opportunities in playoff-implication games.

description: FT-Transformer with learned feature embeddings and MixUp augmentation for robust uncertainty estimation
hypothesis: The previous FT-Transformer underperformed due to insufficient regularization; adding MixUp interpolation between training samples forces smoother decision boundaries and better calibrated probabilities. Learned embeddings for categorical features (player matchups, rest days, back-to-back flags) capture non-linear interactions that tree models miss.

description: Opponent-adjusted four factors with market confidence weighting: Create interaction between (Team_Off_EFF - Opp_Def_EFF_allowed) and closing line volatility (CLV_std_10g), weighted by market steam intensity. Captures when statistical edges align with informed money movement.
hypothesis: Market microstructure signals amplify predictive power of opponent-adjusted efficiency metrics when sharp money is active; CLV volatility acts as confidence filter for statistical edges.

description: Clutch-momentum-market divergence triple: Interaction of 4th quarter net rating trend (last 5 games) with 2nd half line movement direction and pre-game rest differential. Identifies teams whose late-game performance edge is mispriced by markets accounting for fatigue.
hypothesis: Markets underweight clutch momentum when rest asymmetry creates late-game execution disparities; 2H line movement reveals market awareness gap.

description: Referee-player impact Bayesian update: Dynamic prior on free throw rate interaction with referee crew tendency (officiated games FTA/game z-score), updated by player availability volatility (last-minute injury news impact on line). Captures officiating bias amplification under roster uncertainty.
hypothesis: Referee tendencies interact non-linearly with team FT-dependency when roster volatility creates strategic uncertainty; markets slow to adjust to officiating-roster joint effects.

description: LightGBM with quantile-based gradient boosting and custom NBA-specific loss: weighted Brier with asymmetric penalties for home/away misclassification. Uses quantile sketching for robust feature binning on heavy-tailed player efficiency metrics, and implements focal loss variant to down-weight easy schedule-advantage predictions.
hypothesis: Quantile binning handles outlier player performances (load management, injuries) better than uniform binning; asymmetric weighting reflects documented home-court advantage non-stationarity; focal loss improves calibration on imbalanced high-confidence predictions. Expected Brier reduction: 0.006-0.010.

description: Opponent-adjusted four factors momentum: Rolling offensive/defensive rating differentials adjusted by strength of schedule faced, interacted with recent form volatility (std dev of point differential in last 5). Captures whether teams are genuinely improving or benefiting from weak opponents.
hypothesis: Teams showing strong four factors trends against tough schedules with low volatility are more predictable than those with high volatility or weak schedule inflation.

description: Market-clutch microstructure: Closing line value (CLV) interacted with clutch performance differential (clutch net rating vs non-clutch) and rest advantage. Tests whether market inefficiency in pricing late-game execution under fatigue conditions.
hypothesis: CLV signals are amplified when well-rested clutch teams face fatigued opponents with poor late-game execution, creating exploitable mispricing.

description: Referee-style matchup asymmetry: Interaction between referee crew tendency (offensive foul rate, pace impact) and team stylistic fit (fast break frequency vs half-court efficiency). Tests whether specific crew-team combinations create systematic prediction edges.
hypothesis: Fast-break-heavy teams under crews that call fewer offensive fouls and allow higher pace show systematic overperformance vs market expectations.

description: FT-Transformer with learned embedding initialization from player career trajectories and game context tokens. Pre-trains entity embeddings on historical player performance curves then fine-tunes with transformer layers attending across stacked feature embeddings, using Mixup between similar game states and Label Smoothing for calibration.
hypothesis: Pre-trained player trajectory embeddings will provide superior initialization for the FT-Transformer compared to random embeddings, enabling the model to generalize to rare lineup combinations by leveraging historical player similarity, while transformer self-attention captures latent team chemistry and matchup-specific tactical adjustments invisible to tree models.

description: Deep stacking ensemble with uncertainty-calibrated base learners and a differentiable meta-learner. Base layer: XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, TabNet, FT-Transformer each trained with Monte Carlo dropout or quantile regression to output prediction distributions. Meta-learner: small MLP with attention over base predictions, trained to minimize proper scoring rules (Brier/Log-loss) rather than MSE, with explicit regularization against base learner correlation.
hypothesis: Explicit uncertainty quantification at the base level combined with a meta-learner trained on proper scoring rules will achieve superior calibration and Brier score compared to previous stacking approaches, by learning when each model type is trustworthy (e.g., FT-Transformer for novel matchups, tree models for historical rivalries) and discounting correlated errors among similar base learners.

description: Opponent-adjusted four factors momentum divergence: rolling EMA of (team_four_factor - opponent_allowed_four_factor) weighted by strength of schedule, crossed with market line movement direction
hypothesis: Teams showing improving opponent-adjusted efficiency metrics against tough schedules, when diverging from market line movement (steam vs. CLV), indicate model-market inefficiency exploitable for edge

description: Clutch referee-player impact microstructure: referee foul rate tendency in close games (within 5, last 6 min) interacted with player clutch free throw generation and market overreaction to late line moves
hypothesis: Specific referee crews amplify or suppress clutch free throw attempts; when combined with high-clutch-usage players and sharp market movement against public, creates predictable variance in late-game scoring

description: Venue-schedule fatigue decay with market absorption: back-to-back rest differential combined with travel distance and altitude change, interacted with market opening line efficiency (CLV capture rate)
hypothesis: Extreme schedule disadvantages (B2B + travel + altitude) are partially priced but market absorption lags; teams with high CLV capture rates in these spots indicate systematic undervaluation of fatigue effects

description: Rest-schedule-market microstructure triple: Interaction of rest advantage, schedule density (games in last 7 days), and closing line value direction. Isolates fatigue effects when market fails to fully price schedule context.
hypothesis: Rest advantages compound with schedule density in non-linear ways that markets underweight, especially when CLV contradicts public betting patterns (steam against sharp money). The triple interaction captures hidden fatigue premium.

description: Referee-clutch-player impact Bayesian ensemble: Dynamic posterior updating of player impact estimates based on referee foul-calling tendencies in clutch situations, weighted by game leverage.
hypothesis: Referee-specific clutch foul rates interact with player free throw dependency and clutch usage to create predictable scoring environment shifts. Bayesian updating allows rapid adaptation to referee-specific variance that static features miss.

description: FT-Transformer with learned embedding interactions for tabular game state features: Replaces gradient boosting with attention-based architecture that learns contextual relationships between team stats, player availability, and market signals without manual feature engineering
hypothesis: Self-attention mechanisms will capture non-linear interactions between sparse categorical features (player injuries, rest days, back-to-backs) and continuous features (rolling efficiencies) that tree ensembles miss, particularly for edge cases like rare lineup combinations

description: TabNet with sparse attention and sequential decision steps for interpretable game outcome prediction: Uses attention masks to select relevant features per game instance, enabling model to focus on situational signals (clutch performance vs. blowout dynamics)
hypothesis: Feature selection sparsity will improve generalization on out-of-distribution games (playoffs, unusual rest patterns) by preventing overfitting to regular-season correlations, while sequential attention steps mirror human analyst decision-making

description: Clutch referee matchup Bayesian updating with venue altitude interaction: posterior distribution of team clutch performance (last 5 min, within 5) updated with referee-specific foul rate tendencies, moderated by venue altitude effects on shooting fatigue. Captures unpriced environmental-interaction effects.
hypothesis: Referee clutch foul propensity interacts nonlinearly with altitude—high-altitude venues amplify shooting variance, making referee control of game flow more impactful. Markets underprice this three-way interaction.

description: Evaluating the performance of CatBoost with hyperparameter tuning and feature engineering
hypothesis: CatBoost with optimized hyperparameters and feature selection will improve predictive accuracy

description: Opponent-adjusted four factors momentum: Rolling offensive/defensive rating differentials adjusted by opponent strength, interacted with 3-game momentum slope. Captures whether teams are genuinely improving or beating weak opponents.
hypothesis: Raw efficiency stats are misleading without opponent context; combining opponent-adjusted metrics with momentum direction separates signal from schedule noise

description: Market microstructure regime detection: CLV deviation from opening line crossed with steam movement velocity and time-of-day line volatility. Identifies sharp vs. public money periods.
hypothesis: Line movement characteristics contain information about market efficiency regimes; sharp money periods have different predictive value than public chase periods

description: Clutch-referee-player impact Bayesian stack: Posterior probability of clutch performance adjusted by referee foul-call tendency and top-3 player availability volatility.
hypothesis: Clutch performance is non-stationary and referee-dependent; Bayesian updating with player availability uncertainty improves late-game predictions

description: CatBoost with ordered boosting and symmetric trees for NBA tabular data with heavy categorical features (team IDs, player matchups, referee crews). Uses native handling of categorical variables without one-hot encoding to preserve team/player hierarchies and reduce overfitting on rare matchup combinations.
hypothesis: Ordered boosting reduces target leakage common in gradient boosting; symmetric trees + native categorical support will better capture team-specific momentum and lineup chemistry patterns that FT-Transformer and TabNet may overcomplicate.

description: MLP with residual connections, LayerNorm, and learned positional embeddings for temporal sequences of game states. Processes 5-game rolling windows of team statistics through depth-4 network with Swish activation and dropout scheduling.
hypothesis: Residual MLP with proper normalization can learn stable nonlinear interactions between momentum features and rest advantages that tree models split coarsely; temporal positional embeddings capture recency effects without manual decay engineering.

description: Heterogeneous stacking ensemble with tiered meta-learning: Level-0 uses LightGBM (fast patterns), CatBoost (categorical depth), and FT-Transformer (embedding interactions). Level-1 meta-learner is Ridge with prediction variance weighting; final calibration via isotonic regression on holdout season.
hypothesis: Diverse base learners capture complementary error modes—trees for structured patterns, transformer for latent player synergies. Variance-weighted meta-learner downweights uncertain base predictions; isotonic calibration corrects systematic overconfidence from any single model type.

description: Opponent-adjusted four factors EMA divergence with market line movement absorption
hypothesis: Teams showing improving true shooting and defensive efficiency (opponent-adjusted) via EMA, but with market line moving against them, indicates mispricing. The interaction captures when fundamentals diverge from market perception.

description: Clutch player impact microstructure with referee foul rate regime switching
hypothesis: Star player clutch usage (last 5 min, within 5 pts) interacts with referee foul calling tightness in non-clutch periods. Referees who call fewer fouls early allow more physical play that benefits certain clutch player archetypes.

description: Rest-schedule Bayesian updating with venue altitude and steam move direction
hypothesis: Fatigue from schedule density updates prior on team performance, but altitude effects are non-linear and interact with rest days. When steam moves align with altitude-rest advantage (e.g., bet on well-rested team at altitude), signal strengthens.

description: Clutch player impact microstructure with referee crew tenure interaction. Measures star player usage and efficiency in high-leverage moments (last 5 min, within 5 pts) adjusted for referee crew experience and foul-calling consistency, capturing how veteran officiating crews manage end-of-game star dynamics differently.
hypothesis: Referee crews with high tenure reduce home-court clutch advantage by standardizing whistle patterns, creating exploitable market inefficiencies when star-heavy teams face inexperienced crews on road.

description: Rest-schedule density Bayesian updating with market steam detection. Quantifies cumulative fatigue from games-in-N-nights and travel miles, dynamically updating win probability priors based on real-time line movement velocity and volume to identify when market overreacts or underreacts to schedule spots.
hypothesis: Market steam moves on rest advantages are systematically miscalibrated for teams with hidden schedule resilience (deep rotation, altitude training) or hidden fragility (star dependency, back-to-back patterns).

description: Opponent-adjusted rolling four factors z-score divergence crossed with closing line value momentum decay
hypothesis: Teams showing improving fundamental efficiency (opponent-adjusted) against deteriorating market confidence (CLV decay) indicate mispricing; the interaction captures when market lags true form shifts

description: Referee crew clutch foul rate differential interacting with player impact load management fatigue index
hypothesis: High-stakes clutch situations with whistle-happy crews disproportionately punish fatigued star-heavy teams; the interaction reveals hidden penalty variance not priced by market

description: Venue altitude rest disadvantage Bayesian updating with steam move direction and schedule density clustering
hypothesis: Altitude effects compound non-linearly with cumulative schedule load; when sharp money (steam) contradicts public rest narrative, Bayesian updating on clustered schedule density captures true fatigue state

description: FT-Transformer with learned embeddings for player lineup chemistry and opponent defensive scheme matchups, processing tabular features through transformer attention blocks to capture non-linear feature interactions that tree models miss
hypothesis: Neural attention mechanisms will better model complex synergies between lineup composition, defensive schemes, and situational contexts (clutch, back-to-back, altitude) that tree ensembles partition coarsely

description: CatBoost with ordered boosting and symmetric trees, leveraging native categorical handling for player IDs, team matchups, and referee crews without manual encoding, with MSE loss for probabilistic calibration
hypothesis: Ordered boosting reduces prediction shift on small NBA samples; symmetric trees provide regularization; native categorical support eliminates encoding leakage for player/crew identifiers that one-hot trees fragment

description: Hierarchical stacking ensemble with tiered meta-learners: level-0 trains diverse base models (XGB, LGBM, CatBoost, TabNet) on stratified game-type folds; level-1 meta-learner (ridge with calibration) weights by recent Brier performance; level-2 gates predictions by game context (regular season vs. playoff)
hypothesis: Hierarchical stacking reduces overfitting through nested cross-validation while context-gated final layer adapts ensemble weights to structural regime shifts between regular season and playoff basketball

description: Clutch referee bias Bayesian updating: posterior probability of home team free throw advantage in clutch (last 5 min, within 5 pts) based on referee crew historical clutch foul differential, updated with season-to-date crew performance, interacting with home team clutch free throw rate differential
hypothesis: Referee clutch tendencies are sticky but underweighted by markets; Bayesian updating captures true crew bias faster than rolling averages, and interaction with team clutch execution creates nonlinear edge in tight games

description: Steam-movement venue fatigue compound: absolute line movement in final 2 hours (steam) multiplied by altitude-adjusted rest disadvantage (back-to-back + altitude differential), interacting with team depth metric (bench minutes share) to capture when thin rosters amplify market overreactions to schedule spots
hypothesis: Market steam often overreacts to surface-level news while ignoring schedule/venue context; depth moderates fatigue impact, creating exploitable dislocations when steam moves against altitude-rest disadvantaged teams with shallow benches

description: Investigating the impact of FT-Transformer with multi-task learning on NBA predictions
hypothesis: FT-Transformer with multi-task learning will reduce Brier score by jointly learning player and team embeddings and adapting to different game scenarios

description: Evaluating the performance of CatBoost with gradient-based hyperparameter optimization for NBA predictions
hypothesis: CatBoost with gradient-based hyperparameter optimization will decrease Brier score by efficiently searching the hyperparameter space and leveraging ordered boosting

description: Market microstructure regime detection: CLV efficiency ratio (closing line value captured vs. available) crossed with steam movement clustering and venue fatigue, identifying when market movements contain genuine information vs. noise
hypothesis: Not all line movements are equal; CLV efficiency combined with steam clustering patterns and venue context separates informed money from public bias, creating situational edge detection

description: Clutch referee-player archetype interaction: Bayesian posterior of referee foul-calling tightness in clutch updated with player-specific free throw dependency and opponent clutch defensive discipline
hypothesis: Clutch outcomes depend on hidden interactions between referee tendencies and player archetypes; tight refs favor FT-dependent scorers, loose refs favor physical finishers, creating exploitable situational mismatches

description: MLP with residual connections, layer normalization, and learnable feature gating for robust NBA prediction
hypothesis: A carefully regularized deep MLP with feature gating will generalize better than tree ensembles on our small-sample NBA data by avoiding greedy split biases, with residual connections enabling effective training of deeper architectures that capture hierarchical team strength representations
